items.title: Rudy Mazzari Interview, 1959-11-06
items.q: I remember one time, he was, every time he came to the bass passages... he would just say, bass is too loud... Szyzki's already been back with him. And Heifetz is looking toward the basses... Szyzki's arguing with him

ctx.x: Did Hill, uh, let's see, did Heifetz ever play with you when you were there? Oh, in, in Indianapolis? Uh-huh.

Oh, yes. And how? Heifetz played many times. I remember, he used to come every year. In fact, I remember one year, we're scheduled to do a Beethoven violin concerto. And, uh, of course, uh, Szyzki always had to rehearse the orchestra part first. Very important, you know. I remember one time, he was, every time he came to the bass passages, which are very prominent in Beethoven, he would just say, bass is too loud, bass is too loud. So he got us cut down to a whisper. That's a great idea. All right.
